sources.title: AWS Certified Cloud Practitioner (CLF-C02) Exam Guide, Version 1.0
sources.note: Domains, weights, task statements, format and scoring transcribed from the official PDF (pages 1-13, appendices A-B). Guide footer reads 'Version 1.0 CLF-C02'. AWS may publish a newer guide; re-check https://aws.amazon.com/certification/certified-cloud-practitioner/ before relying on weights. The `scope` arrays below are CONDENSED from the guide's 'Knowledge of / Skills in' bullets (pages 4-13): service and concept names only, no new claims.

exam.name: AWS Certified Cloud Practitioner
exam.passMarkNote: Official pass mark is a scaled score of 700 on a 100-1000 scale (compensatory scoring: only the overall result matters). The raw-percentage equivalent is not published, so 70% is a PROXY for display on mock results only.
exam.readinessTargetNote: Your own per-exam target for dashboard/map status (default 80%). Not a vendor figure.
exam.unscoredNote: 15 unscored questions are not identified on the real exam. Unanswered = incorrect; no penalty for guessing.

questionTypes.single: Multiple choice: 1 correct response, 3 distractors (4 options).
questionTypes.multi: Multiple response: 2 or more correct responses out of 5 or more options.

objectives.title: Define the benefits of the AWS Cloud.
scope: Value proposition of the AWS Cloud
Economies of scale (e.g. cost savings)
Global infrastructure benefits (speed of deployment, global reach)
High availability, elasticity, agility

objectives.title: Identify design principles of the AWS Cloud.
scope: AWS Well-Architected Framework
Six pillars: operational excellence, security, reliability, performance efficiency, cost optimization, sustainability
Differences between the pillars

objectives.title: Understand the benefits of and strategies for migration to the AWS Cloud.
scope: Cloud adoption strategies
AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (AWS CAF) benefits (reduced business risk, improved ESG performance, increased revenue, increased operational efficiency)
Migration strategies (e.g. database replication, AWS Snowball)
Resources that support the migration journey

objectives.title: Understand concepts of cloud economics.
scope: Fixed vs variable costs
On-premises cost components
Licensing strategies (Bring Your Own License vs included)
Rightsizing
Automation benefits (e.g. AWS CloudFormation)
Managed services (e.g. Amazon RDS, Amazon ECS, Amazon EKS, Amazon DynamoDB)

objectives.title: Understand the AWS shared responsibility model.
scope: Components of the shared responsibility model
Customer responsibilities
AWS responsibilities
Shared responsibilities
How responsibilities shift by service (e.g. Amazon RDS, AWS Lambda, Amazon EC2)

objectives.title: Understand AWS Cloud security, governance, and compliance concepts.
scope: Where to find compliance information (AWS Artifact, AWS Compliance)
Securing resources (Amazon Inspector, AWS Security Hub, Amazon GuardDuty, AWS Shield)
Encryption in transit and at rest
Governance/compliance services: Amazon CloudWatch (monitoring), AWS CloudTrail, AWS Audit Manager, AWS Config (auditing), access reports
Where to capture and locate security-related logs
Compliance requirements vary among AWS services

objectives.title: Identify AWS access management capabilities.
scope: AWS IAM: users, groups, custom and managed policies, least privilege
Root user: importance of protecting it, tasks only root can perform, protection methods
MFA, IAM Identity Center, cross-account IAM roles
Access keys, password policies, credential storage (AWS Secrets Manager, AWS Systems Manager)
Federated identity management

objectives.title: Identify components and resources for security.
scope: Security features/services: security groups, network ACLs, AWS WAF
Third-party security products in AWS Marketplace
Where AWS security information lives: AWS Knowledge Center, AWS Security Center, AWS Security Blog
AWS Trusted Advisor for identifying security issues

objectives.title: Define methods of deploying and operating in the AWS Cloud.
scope: Ways to access/provision: APIs, SDKs, CLI, Management Console, infrastructure as code
One-time operations vs repeatable processes
Deployment models: cloud, hybrid, on-premises
Connectivity: AWS VPN, AWS Direct Connect, public internet

objectives.title: Define the AWS global infrastructure.
scope: Regions, Availability Zones, edge locations and how they relate
High availability via multiple AZs; AZs do not share single points of failure
When to use multiple Regions (disaster recovery, business continuity, low latency, data sovereignty)
Edge benefits: Amazon CloudFront, AWS Global Accelerator
AWS Wavelength Zones, AWS Local Zones

objectives.title: Identify AWS compute services.
scope: EC2 instance types (e.g. compute optimized, storage optimized)
Containers: Amazon ECS, Amazon EKS
Serverless compute: AWS Fargate, AWS Lambda
Auto scaling provides elasticity
Purpose of load balancers

objectives.title: Identify AWS database services.
scope: EC2-hosted databases vs AWS managed databases
Relational: Amazon RDS, Amazon Aurora
NoSQL: Amazon DynamoDB
Memory-based databases
Migration tools: AWS DMS, AWS Schema Conversion Tool

objectives.title: Identify AWS network services.
scope: VPC components (subnets, gateways)
VPC security: network ACLs, security groups
Amazon Route 53
Edge services: Amazon CloudFront, AWS Global Accelerator
Connectivity to AWS: AWS VPN, AWS Direct Connect

objectives.title: Identify AWS storage services.
scope: Object storage uses; Amazon S3 storage classes
Block storage: Amazon EBS, instance store
File services: Amazon EFS, Amazon FSx
Cached file systems: AWS Storage Gateway
Lifecycle policies
AWS Backup

objectives.title: Identify AWS artificial intelligence and machine learning (AI/ML) services and analytics services.
scope: AI/ML services and tasks: Amazon SageMaker, Amazon Lex, Amazon Kendra
Analytics: Amazon Athena, Amazon Kinesis, AWS Glue, Amazon QuickSight

objectives.title: Identify services from other in-scope AWS service categories.
scope: Application integration: Amazon EventBridge, Amazon SNS, Amazon SQS
Business applications: Amazon Connect, Amazon SES
Customer engagement: AWS Activate for Startups, AWS IQ, AWS Managed Services (AMS), AWS Support
Developer tools: AWS AppConfig, AWS Cloud9, AWS CloudShell, AWS CodeArtifact, AWS CodeBuild, AWS CodeCommit, AWS CodeDeploy, AWS CodePipeline, AWS CodeStar, AWS X-Ray
End-user computing: Amazon AppStream 2.0, Amazon WorkSpaces, Amazon WorkSpaces Web
Frontend web and mobile: AWS Amplify, AWS AppSync
IoT: AWS IoT Core, AWS IoT Greengrass

objectives.title: Compare AWS pricing models.
scope: Compute purchasing options: On-Demand, Reserved Instances, Spot Instances, Savings Plans, Dedicated Hosts, Dedicated Instances, Capacity Reservations
Reserved Instance flexibility and behavior in AWS Organizations
Data transfer charges (incoming/outgoing, cross-Region, same Region)
Pricing for storage options and tiers

objectives.title: Understand resources for billing, budget, and cost management.
scope: AWS Budgets, AWS Cost Explorer, AWS Billing Conductor
AWS Pricing Calculator
AWS Organizations consolidated billing and cost allocation
Cost allocation tags and AWS Cost and Usage Report

objectives.title: Identify AWS technical resources and AWS Support options.
scope: Official docs, whitepapers, blogs; AWS Prescriptive Guidance, AWS Knowledge Center, AWS re:Post
AWS Support plans: Developer, Business, Enterprise On-Ramp, Enterprise; AWS Support Center
AWS Trusted Advisor, AWS Health Dashboard, AWS Health API (monitoring/cost optimization)
AWS Trust and Safety team (report abuse)
AWS Partner Network: AWS Marketplace, ISVs, system integrators; partner benefits
AWS Professional Services, AWS Solutions Architects
